# Webhook events, bot statuses and real-time data

How a bot reports what happens. Branch on `bot_event` (fall back to `event`). Sources are linked in each section.

## Envelope

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| event | Delivery name. Same as bot_event except on an ending, where it is always bot.stopped. |
| bot_event | The specific event. Branch on this; fall back to event when it is missing (resends, older payloads). |
| bot_id | The bot. |
| bot_status | Status at this point. Compare case-insensitively (Error, ERROR, Failed, FAILED). |
| message | Human text. Failures start with Error: (bot could not continue) or Failed: (meeting, host or lobby decided). |
| status_code | A hint, not the outcome (200 or 500). Some endings omit it. |
| timestamp | ISO 8601 on status events; some post-call events omit it; changes on resend. |
| custom_attributes | Echo of what you set on create_bot. |
| scheduled_join_time | Only on bot.scheduled. |
| failure_reason | Google Meet only, on bot.failed when the meeting blocked the join. |

Source: https://docs.meetstream.ai/guides/webhooks/webhooks-and-events

## Lifecycle

bot.scheduled (only with join_at) → `bot.joining` → `bot.in_waiting_room` → `bot.inmeeting` → bot.recording_permission_allowed | bot.recording_permission_denied (Zoom only) → `bot.recording` → `bot.leaving` → one ending: event bot.stopped → post-call events (any order) → bot.done (last) → data_deletion (later)

- bot.joining can arrive more than once for scheduled bots.
- bot.in_waiting_room is sent even when the bot is admitted at once.
- bot.inmeeting arrives at most once per bot.

Source: https://docs.meetstream.ai/guides/webhooks/webhooks-and-events

## Endings

Every ending arrives once with `event: "bot.stopped"`. The cause is `bot_event`.

| bot_event | bot_status | status_code | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| bot.stopped | Stopped | 200 | Meeting ended, everyone left, automatic leave, removed through the API, Zoom recording permission denied or timed out |
| bot.kicked | Stopped | 200 | A host or participant removed the bot (same bot_status as a clean exit) |
| bot.denied | Denied | 500 | The host rejected the join, or the platform refused |
| bot.notallowed | NotAllowed | 500 | Not admitted before automatic_leave.waiting_room_timeout |
| bot.failed | Error / ERROR / Failed / FAILED | use bot_event | Could not join or continue |

- A bot removed before it joins moves to Stopped, and on Zoom and Google Meet no ending event follows: mark it ended when remove_bot succeeds.
- Many Zoom join failures end as Stopped: success needs bot.inmeeting and an empty ErrorReason on /detail.
- A bot stuck in Joining for about 60 minutes ends NotAllowed (JoinTimeout).
- Google Meet failure_reason values: invalid_meeting_link, meeting_not_started, meeting_ended, meeting_restricted, sign_in_required, google_sign_in_failed, cant_join_call, admission_not_confirmed.

Sources: https://docs.meetstream.ai/guides/webhooks/webhooks-and-events, https://docs.meetstream.ai/guides/reference/bot-status-and-error-codes

## After the call

Any order; `bot.done` is always last.

| bot_event | Field | status_code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| audio.processed | audio_status Success | 200 | Mixed audio ready: GET /api/v1/bots/{bot_id}/get_audio |
| audio.skipped | audio_status Skipped | 200 | No audio captured (no_audio_reason) |
| audio.failed | audio_status Failed | 400 or 500 | Audio processing failed |
| video.processed | video_status Success | 200 | GET /api/v1/bots/{bot_id}/get_video |
| video.failed | video_status Failed | 500 |  |
| transcription.processed | transcript_status Success | 200 | Post-call transcript ready (transcript_id: read /detail) |
| transcription.skipped | transcript_status Skipped | 200 | No audio or no valid provider config |
| transcription.not_required | transcript_status Skipped | 200 | No post-call transcription configured |
| transcription.failed | transcript_status Failed | 500 | Re-run: POST /api/v1/bots/{bot_id}/transcribe |
| bot.done | bot_status | 200 | Everything finished (finished, not succeeded); also sent for bots that never got in |

Source: https://docs.meetstream.ai/guides/webhooks/webhooks-and-events

## Other events

| Event | Meaning |
|---|---|
| bot.error | Non-fatal in-meeting problem (for example a live transcription provider failed), or a scheduled bot rejected at start (ScheduledDispatchRejected, StorageValidationFailed, InsufficientCredits). Workspace endpoints only. |
| agent_error | MIA voice agent problem. Workspace endpoints only. |
| participant_events.join / .leave / .chat_message | Real-time participant events. Subscribe with recording_config.realtime_endpoints. |
| participant_events.raise_hand / .lower_hand | Google Meet and Zoom; only to realtime_endpoints that list them, never to workspace webhooks. |
| manifest.completed / .skipped / .failed | Audio manifest processing. |
| usage.milestone_* / usage.inactive_* / usage.weekly_summary | Account usage notices. Workspace endpoints only. |
| bot.uploading / bot.transcriptionready | Informational post-call events. |
| data_deletion | Media deleted (retention or DELETE /api/v1/bots/{bot_id}/delete); status becomes MediaExpired. |

Unknown event names can appear: ignore them, do not fail.

Sources: https://docs.meetstream.ai/guides/webhooks/webhooks-and-events, https://docs.meetstream.ai/guides/features/participants-and-speaker-timeline, https://docs.meetstream.ai/guides/reference/bot-status-and-error-codes

## Delivery

- Workspace endpoints (dashboard, up to 10, event filter) are signed: X-MeetStream-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed with the endpoint secret>. X-MeetStream-Timestamp is not part of the signed content.
- Per-bot callback_url deliveries are not signed. Live-transcript POSTs are not signed: put a secret token in the URL and check that bot_id is yours.
- Each event is delivered once, with no automatic retry. Resend by hand from the endpoint's Logs tab (up to 10 times).
- Reply 2xx within 5 seconds, then process. Poll GET /bots/{bot_id}/status as a fallback for bots in Joining or Scheduled.
- De-duplicate on (bot_id, bot_event or event). Do not de-duplicate bot.joining or participant_events.* on that key (repeats are normal).
- Post-call events arrive in any order; bot.done is last.
- transcript_id is in no webhook: read it from the create_bot response or GET /bots/{bot_id}/detail.
- Since 12 Nov 2026, post-call webhooks go only to public addresses.

Sources: https://docs.meetstream.ai/guides/webhooks/webhooks-and-events, https://docs.meetstream.ai/guides/webhooks/workspace-webhooks, https://docs.meetstream.ai/guides/webhooks/webhook-signature-verification, https://docs.meetstream.ai/guides/transcription-recordings/live-transcription

## Live transcript

Sent to `live_transcription_required.webhook_url`.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| bot_id | The bot |
| speakerName, speakerId | Who spoke (exact only on Zoom) |
| transcript | Text for this POST |
| utterance | Sentence mode: same as transcript |
| words[] | word, start, end, confidence, punctuated_word |
| end_of_turn, turn_order | Turn markers |
| transcription_mode | raw, word_level or sentence |
| timestamp | When the result was produced |
| custom_attributes | Echoed from create_bot |

- No event key in the payload.
- One streaming provider per bot.
- A streaming provider needs live_transcription_required.webhook_url (400 without it).

Source: https://docs.meetstream.ai/guides/transcription-recordings/live-transcription

## Live audio and control socket

- The bot connects to your WebSocket server (template a server, not a client).
- First message: JSON ready. Then binary PCM16 little-endian frames.
- Byte 0 is the frame type: 0x01 = 48 kHz mono; 0x04 = header with sample rate and channel count (Zoom uses 32 kHz). Google Meet sends both: check byte 0 on every frame.

**Control socket**

- socket_connection_url: send sendaudio, sendmsg (include message and msg), sendimg, interrupt, resume_audio.
- On Zoom and Teams, interrupt blocks later audio until resume_audio.

**Not live**

- live_video_required is not implemented.
- Per-participant audio and video are files after the call.

Sources: https://docs.meetstream.ai/guides/websockets/real-time-audio-streaming, https://docs.meetstream.ai/guides/websockets/meeting-control-patterns
